messages:
maria: seeing a weird p99 TTFT jump for token-level traces in us-west-2 around 00:20 UTC, stepping from ~220ms -> ~820ms for short prompts

sam: on it, can you paste the grafana panel?

maria: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ttft/token-p99?orgId=1&from=now-2h&to=now — spike aligns with a network flurry on nodepool-west2-gpu-b

jing: pulling logs + prometheus: run this PromQL to validate the burst and any packet drops:
```
sum(rate(tcp_retransmit_total{region="us-west-2"}[5m])) by (instance)
```

ryan: also check kernel NIC errors: `kubectl -n infra exec -it node-exporter-... -- cat /proc/net/dev` for the node in question

olga: FYI we had an infra scaling event ~00:15 where autoscaler tried to deprovision 2 old-gpu nodes then failed and retried. possible transient congestion?

maria: prom query shows retransmit spikes on ip-10-0-32-11 and ip-10-0-48-3 starting 00:18, matches grafana overlay with TTFT p99

sam: can we correlate with KV cache miss rate? maybe traffic pattern caused more cache misses -> higher tokens/sec -> larger networking bursts

jing: KV cache hit ratio from logs: `kv_cache_hit_ratio{shard="west2-a"}` dropped from 0.92 -> 0.69 at 00:17

ryan: that explains higher egress between shards. also noticed MTU mismatch warnings on the kube-proxy logs on ip-10-0-48-3 around same time

olga: action idea: tune alert to include correlated signals (p99 TTFT + tcp_retransmits + kv_cache_drop) so we avoid noisy all-clear flapping. currently alert fires on p99 alone

sam: agree. new alert proposal (temp):
```
alert: TokenTTFTNetworkSaturation
expr: increase(p99_token_ttft[5m]) > 2 and sum(rate(tcp_retransmit_total[5m])) by (region) > 5 and avg(kv_cache_hit_ratio) by (region) < 0.75
for: 10m
```

maria: also recommend adding a node-level egress rate panel to token dashboards and surface the node pool names (old-gpu vs new-gpu)

ryan: on provisioning — we still have 12% oversubscription on the old-gpu pool; either we move short-LLM traffic to new-quantized pool or reserve a small burst capacity to avoid these autoscaler churn windows

olga: cost callout: reserving 2x small-GPU burst nodes will add ~$6k/month but should reduce p99 SLO violations during scaling thrash. worth for next sprint?

maria: +1 — set an experiment for 2 weeks, monitor tokens/sec per-node and p99. If improvement, can propose reserved commit to finance

infra-bot: created runbook task TICKET-4581: "Investigate west2 TTFT p99 spike + network retransmits" assigned to eng-sre, due in 3 days

sam: for immediate mitigation I rolled out a kube-proxy MTU config tweak to 1500 on the affected pool and bumped kube-scheduler eviction thresholds. will watch for recurrence

jing: keeping a 12h recording rule that captures p99 slices by prompt-length would help drilldowns later — creating PR for that

maria: cool. next steps: (1) enable the alert proposal as alert-manager suppression for noisy windows, (2) run 2-week reserved burst experiment, (3) add egress per-node panel, (4) link runbook from dashboard. tagging @oncall for visibility

sam: noted. will follow up with a short postmortem if we see more than 3 repeats in 72h

maria: thanks team :thumbsup:
